summary: The study describes the use of atomic layer epitaxy (ALE) to grow CdS layers on a ZnSe(100) substrate using dimethylcadmium (DMCd) and hydrogen sulfide (H2S) as precursors. The process involves sequential surface reactions, leading to self-limiting growth and the formation of a sulfur-hydride terminated surface. The results are supported by NEXAFS spectroscopy and TPD studies, which confirm the surface chemistry and growth mechanism.
evidence: Atomic layer epitaxy (ALE) using a binary reaction sequence of the precursors dimethylcadmium (DMCd) and hydrogen sulfide (H2S) is shown to produce epitaxial layers of CdS on a ZnSe(100) substrate. The results are supported by NEXAFS spectroscopy and TPD studies, which confirm the surface chemistry and growth mechanism.
